problem.headline: You do everything right. And something is still missing.

cards.title: You're looking for validation — and don't notice it.
cards.body: When success comes, you feel good for a moment. When it doesn't, you collapse inside. And you compensate with more performance.

cards.title: You say yes when you mean no.
cards.body: You adapt, avoid conflict, make compromises that leave you hollow by evening. You betray yourself without noticing.

cards.title: You don't know what you actually want.
cards.body: Career, relationship, where to live — you wait for the moment of clarity that never comes. Because you never learned to listen to yourself.

approach.body1: Most men's coaches work on behavior. More discipline. More routines. Better pickup lines. That works for two weeks. Then you fall back — and you believe you've failed.
approach.body2: My approach: we work on the psychological structure underneath. Why do you do what you do? Why do you avoid what you avoid? What are you protecting without noticing?
approach.body3: The result isn't a 'new you.' It's a clearer one. One that decides from itself — not from the fear of being rejected.

items.title: You write to me.
items.body: You answer the five questions below and send them to mail@danielhanke.com. I respond within 48 hours.

items.title: I reply — honestly.
items.body: If I believe I can help you, I'll suggest dates and send you the payment details. If not, I'll tell you that too — and, where possible, point you to an alternative.

items.title: You book — and we work.
items.body: One hour 120 €, paid in advance by bank transfer. No minimum term, no packages. We meet every 1–2 weeks, 60 minutes, via Zoom. Between sessions: concrete exercises, brief check-ins by email if you get stuck. Confidential, no notes shared with third parties.

benefits.eyebrow: What you get out of it

items.title: You understand why you do what you do.
items.body: We work on the patterns that drive your behavior. Once you see them, you stop sabotaging yourself — not through discipline, but through clarity.

items.title: You decide from yourself.
items.body: Career, relationship, where to live — you stop waiting for the right moment. Because you've learned to trust yourself.

items.title: You become genuinely present in relationships.
items.body: With women, friends, family. You stop protecting yourself, and you actually show up. That changes who responds to you — and how.

items.title: You finally feel like a man.
items.body: Not loud, not hard, not performative. Grounded. Reliable. Clear. Yourself — even when no one's watching.

fit.eyebrow: For whom — and for whom not
forYou: You're between 22 and 38 and live in the German-speaking region.
You function in life — and still feel like something is off.
You've read books, taken courses, tried discipline — and noticed: the problem is deeper.
You're ready to give honest answers, even when they're uncomfortable.
You understand that change takes time — no 30-day challenge.
notForYou: You're in acute psychological crisis (depression, anxiety disorder, trauma, suicidal thoughts). Then you need therapy, not coaching. I'm happy to help you find someone.
You're looking for pickup tricks or 'alpha frames'.
You expect me to tell you what to do.
You're not ready to invest in yourself — financially and time-wise.

request.headline: Write me an email. Answer these five questions.
request.body: No scheduling software, no online form. An honest email filters better than any tool. Answer as briefly or as fully as it feels right — one line per question is enough, more is fine too.

questions.title: What's going on in your life right now?
What have you tried so far to change it?
What would change concretely if we really moved something in the next 3 months?
Why now?
questions.body: What changed that you're writing today — and not in six months?

questions.title: Availability:
questions.body: Which weekdays and times could you do regularly (every 1–2 weeks, 60 minutes) via Zoom?

request.subtext: I respond within 48 hours — even if the answer is 'no match'. If it fits, I'll send you suggested times and payment details.

items.a: 120 € per hour (60 minutes), paid in advance by bank transfer. No minimum term, no packages, no onboarding fee.

items.q: I have specific questions before booking — can I briefly talk to you?
items.a: Yes. Send me an email to mail@danielhanke.com with your question. If a short call makes sense — e.g. to check compatibility — we'll arrange a 5- to 10-minute phone slot by email. This does not replace coaching and is not the entry into the program, only for targeted clarifications.

items.q: How many sessions do I need?
items.a: It depends on what you want to change. Some men work with me for 6 months, others for two years. There's no minimum term. We decide together after session 4 whether it fits.

items.q: What if I need therapy instead of coaching?
items.a: Then I'll tell you that honestly in my reply to your inquiry. Coaching works on patterns in the here and now. Therapy works on trauma, diagnoses, clinical symptoms. Sometimes you need both.
Yes. We talk every 1–2 weeks — but pauses are fine. I don't work with pressure.

items.q: Why not shorter sessions or groups?
items.a: 60 minutes 1:1 is the smallest meaningful unit. Group coaching is coming later (see Community).

hero.title: Selbstdisziplin 2.0.
hero.subline: The simple path to strong self-discipline and productivity. Not through more willpower — but by learning to direct your motivation. Currently available in German only; an English edition is under consideration.

content.headline: Discipline isn't a character trait. It's a system.
content.body1: Almost everyone knows what they should do to move forward. The problem isn't knowledge — it's that most people lack the self-discipline to actually do it. Not money, not luck, not IQ. Self-discipline is the bottleneck for success.
content.body2: Most books frame discipline as a fight against yourself — willpower you have to muster every morning. Selbstdisziplin 2.0 turns that around: genuinely successful people don't fight. They've learned to direct their motivation, instead of being manipulated by it into temptation.
content.body3: The book lays out the methods. How you bring your brain to your side instead of working against it every day. How you break out of the loop of mediocrity — not by being harder, but by running a better system.

forWhom.headline: Who the book is for
items: You know what you should do — and still don't do it.
You've tried discipline as raw willpower. It drained you.
You want to understand what genuinely successful people do differently — and learn it for yourself.

hero.title: Daniel Hanke.
hero.subline: Psychological counselor. Author. Coach for men who function in life — and not for themselves.

items: Born 1992 in Karlsruhe, currently lives in Leipzig — visually and culturally at home in Berlin.
M.A. Business Psychology and International Management, University of Heidelberg.
NLP Master Practitioner. Certified psychological counselor.
Author of 'Selbstdisziplin 2.0' and several other books.
Managing director of Next Level Education GmbH.

intro.title: How it started.
intro.body1: I was one of those boys. Overprotective mother, absent and choleric father, learned early to play the role that pleases others. At 14 I fell in love at a confirmation with a girl — she flirted with me, I ran away crying. That was the point I understood: something about me doesn't work.
intro.body2: Three years later I secretly attended an NLP seminar in Berlin, against my parents' wishes. It was the first time I acted against their expectation. It didn't 'heal' me. But it opened a door.

detour.title: The long detour.
detour.body1: Acting school in Kiel — dropped out. Teacher training in Tübingen — dropped out. Business psychology in Heidelberg — the best years of my studies. Master in International Management — a burnout I didn't admit for a long time.
detour.body2: After that: my own attempts at self-employment (Einserfabrik, books, a YouTube channel that drifted for years). Street fundraising for Greenpeace. Solar sales at Enpal in Berlin. Six months of sales training that taught me more than ten books. Travel — Thailand, a startup community in Malaysia. Then back.
detour.body3: It wasn't a straight path. It was a path with many wrong decisions — and I tell this not out of shame, but because I believe: anyone who claims to have done everything right is either lying or didn't risk enough.

why.title: Why coaching.
why.body1: At some point it became clear to me: I'd spent my whole life trying to repair something that couldn't be repaired. Only understood. And only what I'd understood, I could let go of.
why.body2: Today I work with men who stand in exactly that place. Who do everything they're supposed to — and don't arrive. I don't give them new tricks. I give them a mirror they can't hold up to themselves. And a sparring partner who doesn't look away when it gets uncomfortable.

get: Honest confrontation when needed — always with respect.
Concrete tools that work between sessions.

keynotes.headline: 5 keynotes I offer
keynotes.intro: Each keynote combines psychological depth with clear language. No motivational show. No worn-out phrases. Topics that hit people inside and move them forward in practice.
keynotes.videoLabel: How this topic sounds from me:

items.title: You're not shy. Your system is protecting you.
items.body: What we often dismiss as weakness — restraint, avoidance, hesitation or insecurity — is often an intelligent protective mechanism that once made sense. This keynote turns shame into understanding and understanding into agency.
items.fit: Men's events, universities, mental-health formats, coaching communities, companies, young professionals.
items.videoTopic: You're not shy. Your system is protecting you.

items.title: The facade holds. The man behind it doesn't.
items.body: On men and high performers who deliver on the outside, function and look strong — but run empty inside. Why more performance doesn't fill the inner hole but often deepens it. And how real inner ground can grow again where functioning has taken over.
items.fit: Companies, leadership offsites, mental-health programs, men's events, universities, HR formats.
items.videoTopic: Approval-seeking, functioning, inner emptiness or self-worth

items.title: The yes that eats you alive.
items.body: People-pleasing isn't kindness. It's often a survival pattern. This keynote shows why adapting protects in the short term but destroys identity, clarity and self-respect over time. Especially relevant for teams, relationships and ambitious people who avoid conflict.
items.fit: Companies, teams, leadership formats, men's groups, coaching events, retreats.
items.videoTopic: People-pleasing, saying no, boundaries or conflict avoidance

items.title: Self-worth that doesn't come from outside.
items.body: As long as self-worth is tied to success, praise, status, dating wins or recognition, every victory is just a rented lease. This keynote shows the path from external validation to inner ground — psychologically grounded, honest, without spiritual clichés.
items.fit: Conferences, men's events, universities, personal development formats, podcasts, companies.
items.videoTopic: Self-worth, validation, success or inner ground

items.title: No alpha, no victim.
items.body: What masculinity can be today — beyond red-pill dogma, victimhood, conformity and the optimization craze. A keynote on strength, vulnerability, boundaries, responsibility and emotional maturity.
items.fit: Men's events, festivals, retreats, podcasts, media formats, psychological conferences.
items.videoTopic: Masculinity, dating, self-respect or emotional maturity

workshops.headline: 3 workshops for real integration
workshops.intro: Workshops aren't talks with a few questions at the end. They're interactive, practical and built for transfer. Participants don't just understand something — they see themselves more clearly and leave with concrete next steps.

items.title: Reading your inner system
items.body: Participants map their own avoidance, protection and adaptation patterns. They recognize why they sidestep, want to please, over-deliver or shut down emotionally in certain situations.
items.result: Every participant leaves with a personal pattern map and concrete options for action.
items.fit: Men's groups, retreats, leadership offsites, universities, coaching communities.

items.title: Saying no without losing yourself
items.body: A practical workshop on boundaries, conflict capacity and clear communication. Not just cognitive but also somatic and emotional. With reflection, role-play and concrete phrasings.
items.result: Participants learn to set boundaries without tipping into hardness, justification or guilt.
items.fit: Teams, companies, leaders, men's groups, relationship contexts, coaching events.

items.title: Self-discipline 2.0 — steer motivation instead of forcing it
items.body: Based on my book „Selbstdisziplin 2.0". This workshop shows why discipline doesn't grow from self-hatred, pressure or motivation, but from identity, structure, emotional clarity and a system that holds on bad days too.
items.result: Participants develop a personal discipline system with concrete routines, triggers, fallback strategies and a clear why.
items.fit: Companies, young professionals, founders, universities, men's groups, productivity events.
